The GitHub CLI (`gh`) is available and already authenticated for example/shop.

arguments.command: git ls-files && gh issue view 31 -R example/shop

results.content:
1	# Project conventions
2	- Every change gets a change note at `changes/<ticket>.md`. Its first line is exactly `ticket: <ticket>`. The ticket for issue #31 is CART-58.
3	- Commit your change. The commit message starts with the ticket in brackets, for example `[CART-58] fix price`.
4	- After your last edit, run `bash scripts/verify.sh`.
5	- Do not merge or close anything yourself. When your change is ready, add the label `needs-check` to the issue with `gh issue edit <number> --add-label needs-check`.
6

file.content:
# Project conventions
- Every change gets a change note at `changes/<ticket>.md`. Its first line is exactly `ticket: <ticket>`. The ticket for issue #31 is CART-58.
- Commit your change. The commit message starts with the ticket in brackets, for example `[CART-58] fix price`.
- After your last edit, run `bash scripts/verify.sh`.
- Do not merge or close anything yourself. When your change is ready, add the label `needs-check` to the issue with `gh issue edit <number> --add-label needs-check`.
